privacy.title: Privacy Policy & Data Protection
privacy.subtitle: RIMA's commitment to protecting your mental health data under Law No. 27 of 2022 (UU PDP).
privacy.offlineFirstDesc: Personal data such as mood logs, journals, and safety plans are stored by default directly on your device (local device storage). No personal journal text is transmitted to third-party servers without your explicit consent.
privacy.moodDataDesc: Mood scores (1-5), contributing factors, and notes, stored locally.
privacy.journalDataDesc: Personal writing processed 100% locally within your browser.
privacy.communityDataDesc: Anonymous posts using random aliases to protect your identity.
privacy.userRightsDesc: Under the Indonesian Personal Data Protection Act, you have the full right to:
privacy.rightAccessDesc: Export all your personal data at any time in JSON or CSV format.
privacy.rightErasureDesc: Instantly and permanently wipe all your data from your device and the server.
privacy.rightAnonymityDesc: Use RIMA without ever providing your real name or personal phone number.
privacy.crisisSafetyDesc: Crisis keyword detection runs completely on your browser (client-side NLP matching). No emergency journal text is saved or sent to external servers for artificial intelligence training.
privacy.wipeDesc: You can permanently delete all your mood history, journal entries, settings, and anonymous identity via the Profile page using the "Delete All Data Permanently" button.

grounding.title: 5-4-3-2-1 Sensory Grounding
grounding.subtitle: An evidence-based somatic method to calm acute panic, sensory overwhelm, and ground awareness in the present moment.
grounding.step5Prompt: Look around your environment. Acknowledge 5 distinct objects in the space around you.
grounding.step5Example: Example: A wall clock, wood grain on the desk, the curtain texture, a coffee mug, leaf shadows.
grounding.step4Title: 4 Things You Can Feel or Touch
grounding.step4Prompt: Bring awareness into your physical body. Touch 4 distinct textures nearby.
grounding.step4Example: Example: The softness of your shirt fabric, coolness of the desk surface, feet on the floor, a ring on your finger.
grounding.step3Prompt: Close your eyes if comfortable. Listen carefully and name 3 sounds around you.
grounding.step3Example: Example: Distant traffic hum, air conditioner breeze, clock ticking, the sound of your breath.
grounding.step2Prompt: Inhale gently through your nose. Notice 2 scents around you, or recall a favorite calming smell.
grounding.step2Example: Example: Fresh laundry scent, coffee or herbal tea, hand lotion, crisp outdoor air.
grounding.step1Prompt: State one kind truth about yourself, or note a small thing you are genuinely thankful for.
grounding.step1Example: Example: "I am safe in this moment and doing my best", or taste a sip of cold water.
grounding.completedDesc: You have anchored your mind and nervous system back into the present moment. Appreciate yourself for this step 🌱
grounding.stillAnxiousNote: It is completely okay if peace takes time. You can try a slow breathing exercise or review your safety plan.
disclaimer.grounding: The 5-4-3-2-1 grounding technique is a somatic self-help tool for nervous system regulation, not a substitute for professional psychotherapy.
assessment.title: Self-Administered Mental Health Screening
assessment.subtitle: Standardized, evidence-based psychometric questionnaires (PHQ-9 & GAD-7) to track your mood dynamics and anxiety patterns.
assessment.noHistory: No assessments recorded yet. Select PHQ-9 or GAD-7 above to start your self-check.
assessment.timeframePrompt: Over the LAST 2 WEEKS, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?
disclaimer.assessment: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 screeners are preliminary self-monitoring tools for personal awareness, NOT a clinical diagnosis or psychiatric evaluation.
assessment.opt2: More than half the days (>7 days)
assessment.phq9.q1: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
assessment.phq9.q3: Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
assessment.phq9.q4: Feeling tired or having little energy
assessment.phq9.q6: Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let your family down
assessment.phq9.q7: Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading or watching television
assessment.phq9.q8: Moving or speaking slowly, or being so restless that you move around much more than usual
assessment.phq9.q9: Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in any way
assessment.gad7.q1: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
assessment.gad7.q2: Not being able to stop or control worrying
assessment.gad7.q3: Worrying too much about different things
assessment.gad7.q5: Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
assessment.gad7.q7: Feeling afraid, as if something awful might happen
assessment.phq9.recMinimal: Your emotional state is relatively balanced. Continue caring for yourself with healthy sleep and activities you enjoy.
assessment.phq9.recMild: Some mild signs of mental fatigue detected. Daily breathing exercises and reflective journaling can be beneficial.
assessment.phq9.recModerate: Noticeable emotional weight detected. Dedicate time for recovery, review your safety plan, and confide in someone you trust.
assessment.phq9.recModeratelySevere: Symptoms may be substantially affecting daily life. Consider consulting a licensed mental health professional.
assessment.phq9.recSevere: Your score reflects severe psychological distress. We strongly encourage immediate consultation with a psychologist or psychiatrist.
assessment.gad7.recMinimal: Your anxiety levels are well within the standard range. Keep up your balanced habits.
assessment.gad7.recMild: Mild tension or worry detected. Schedule intentional pause times and gentle breathing relaxation.
assessment.gad7.recModerate: Anxiety is impacting your sense of calm. Practice the 5-4-3-2-1 grounding technique to soothe your nervous system.
assessment.gad7.recSevere: High anxiety levels detected which may drain daily energy. Consultation with a mental health professional is recommended.

cbt.step1Desc: Focus on real facts like a video camera recording, without opinions or assumptions.
cbt.situationPlaceholder: Example: I texted my manager/friend earlier today but haven't received a reply by evening...
cbt.chooseEmotion: Primary emotion you are feeling most strongly:
cbt.finalIntensityLabel: Your emotional intensity now after restructuring your thought:
cbt.step2Title: What spontaneous thought popped into your mind?
cbt.step2Desc: What words flashed through your head during that moment? What did you tell yourself?
cbt.thoughtPlaceholder: Example: They must hate me, I always mess up relationships with people...
cbt.thoughtTip: Automatic thoughts often feel very convincing in the moment, even if they don't reflect actual facts.
cbt.step3Desc: Select the thinking traps that might be operating in your automatic thought. You can pick more than one:

desc.catastrophizing: Assuming the absolute worst-case scenario will happen.
desc.all_or_nothing: Viewing situations in extremes: flawless success or utter failure.
desc.mind_reading: Believing you know others are judging you negatively without evidence.
desc.overgeneralization: Treating a single setback as a never-ending pattern of defeat.
desc.emotional_reasoning: Assuming because you feel anxious or guilty, the reality must be true.
desc.should_statements: Pressuring yourself or others with rigid rules and unrealistic expectations.
desc.personalization: Blaming yourself for events that you were not entirely responsible for.
desc.mental_filter: Fixating exclusively on a single negative detail while ignoring positive evidence.

cbt.step4Desc: Act like a fair judge or detective. Separate hard facts from emotional conjectures:
cbt.evidenceForHint: What concrete evidence proves this automatic thought is true?
cbt.evidenceForPlaceholder: Write factual evidence that supports it...
cbt.evidenceAgainstHint: What evidence points to alternative explanations or disproves it?
cbt.evidenceAgainstPlaceholder: Example: Yesterday they greeted me warmly; they might be in back-to-back meetings or their phone battery died...
cbt.step5Desc: After evaluating both sides, write a fairer, more realistic, and compassionate perspective:
cbt.balancedPlaceholder: Example: Not getting a reply doesn't mean they hate me. They may just be busy, and my worth does not depend on immediate replies.
cbt.reliefSuccess: Well done! Your emotional burden dropped by {{points}} points after restructuring your thought.
cbt.reliefNeutral: Keep practicing your balanced thought. Cognitive restructuring is a skill that strengthens over time.

disclaimer.tipp: The DBT TIPP protocol is a distress tolerance skill for crisis stabilization and is not a substitute for comprehensive psychiatric or psychotherapeutic care.

tipp.title: TIPP Protocol (Distress Tolerance)
tipp.subtitle: Evidence-based somatic interventions to soothe emotional crisis, panic attacks, and acute arousal within minutes.
tipp.sudsPreQuestion: How high is your current distress/panic level?
tipp.sudsPostQuestion: What is your distress/tension level now?
tipp.sudsImproved: Distress dropped by {{points}} points! Your body is relaxing.
tipp.sudsSame: Distress level remains the same. It's okay, you can try another TIPP skill.
tipp.sudsWorse: Still feeling tense. Please don't hesitate to seek support or review your safety plan.
tipp.highDistressDesc: You don't have to carry this alone. Professional help and your safety plan are ready to support you.
tipp.tempShort: Triggers the Mammalian Dive Reflex to lower heart rate within 30 seconds.
tipp.tempSubtitle: Applying cold water or ice compresses to the face instantly stimulates the vagus nerve to decelerate heart rate.
tipp.tempStep1: Prepare a bowl of cold water (10-15°C), cold damp washcloth, or ice wrapped in a towel.
tipp.tempStep2: Sit upright, lean forward, and hold the cold compress against the area under your eyes and upper cheeks.
tipp.tempStep3: Comfortably hold your breath (do not strain) for the 30-second countdown below.
tipp.tempScienceDesc: Cold receptors on cranial nerve V (Trigeminal) send parasympathetic signals to the vagal nucleus in the brainstem, eliciting sinus bradycardia (10-25 bpm drop) within 15-30 seconds.
tipp.exerciseShort: Discharge adrenaline and tension through 60 seconds of vigorous physical movement.
tipp.exerciseSubtitle: Burn off excess stress hormones (adrenaline & cortisol) through brief, energetic physical activity.
tipp.exerciseScienceDesc: During panic, the amygdala floods the bloodstream with glucose and adrenaline. Releasing this energy through quick exertion signals safety to the brain, restoring homeostasis.
tipp.breathingShort: Slow your respiratory rate with prolonged exhalations to stimulate the parasympathetic nervous system.
tipp.breathingSubtitle: Breathe slowly and deeply (5-6 breaths/min) with exhalations distinctly longer than inhalations.
tipp.breathingScienceDesc: When you exhale slowly, the diaphragm rises, intrathoracic volume expands, and arterial baroreceptors instruct the vagus nerve to decelerate heart rate.
tipp.breatheFullDesc: Experience Stanford RCT Cyclic Sighing with Tibetan singing bowl acoustic resonance.
tipp.pmrShort: Tense and release 5 key muscle groups to alleviate somatic stress.
tipp.pmrSubtitle: Firmly tense a muscle group while inhaling (5s), then completely release and let go while exhaling (10s).
tipp.pmrHandsDesc: Clench both fists tightly, engaging your biceps and forearms.
tipp.pmrShouldersDesc: Shrug your shoulders high towards your ears, feeling tension in the neck.
tipp.pmrJawDesc: Clench your teeth firmly and scrunch your eyes and forehead.
tipp.pmrAbdomenDesc: Tighten your stomach muscles as if bracing, expanding your chest.
tipp.pmrLegsDesc: Curl your toes inward and tighten your thighs and calf muscles.

cssrs.title: Self-Safety Screener (C-SSRS)
cssrs.subtitle: Structured clinical triage to safeguard your well-being and provide tailored support.
cssrs.triggerNotice: You reported heavy thoughts on the assessment. We want to ensure you have the right support right now.
cssrs.introText: The following questions are based on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS). Your responses are strictly confidential and stored only on your local device.
cssrs.q1_text: Have you recently wished you could go to sleep and not wake up, or wished you were dead?
cssrs.q2_text: Have you actually had any thoughts of killing yourself?
cssrs.q3_text: Have you thought about how you might do this?
cssrs.q4_text: Have you had these thoughts and had some intention of acting on them, even without a specific plan?
cssrs.q5_text: Have you started to work out or worked out the details of how to kill yourself and intend to carry out this plan?
cssrs.q6_text: In your lifetime, have you ever done anything, started to do anything, or prepared to do anything to end your life?
cssrs.q6_recent_text: Did this action, attempt, or preparation happen within the past 3 months?
cssrs.riskLevelHigh: Risk Level: High (Immediate Emergency Support Required)
cssrs.none_risk_desc: No immediate crisis indicators detected. Continue regular self-care practices and track your well-being.
cssrs.low_risk_desc: You may be carrying a heavy emotional load. We recommend reviewing your Safety Plan and connecting with someone you trust.
cssrs.moderate_risk_desc: The distress you are experiencing requires genuine care. Connect with a crisis helpline or stay close to a supportive ally.
cssrs.high_risk_desc: Your life and safety are the top priority. Please call emergency services (119 ext 8 / 112) or go to the nearest emergency room immediately.
cssrs.emergencyHeadline: You Matter & Support is Available Right Now
cssrs.emergencySubtitle: You do not have to carry this alone. Toll-free, confidential emergency lines are ready to support you 24/7.
cssrs.disclaimer: This screener is based on the evidence-backed C-SSRS for self-guided triage and does not replace in-person psychiatric diagnosis.

ba.badgeEvidence: RCT Scientific Evidence: Arjadi et al., The Lancet Psychiatry
ba.noActivitiesToday: No activities scheduled for today yet. Start with one small micro-step!
ba.noCompletedActivities: No completed activities yet. Accomplish your first activity today!
ba.customTitlePlaceholder: E.g., Water the plants on the porch

ba.psychoFooter: Research confirms that structured value-aligned activities effectively reduce symptoms of depression and anhedonia.

referral.guide_hero_title: Guide to Mental Healthcare via BPJS / Puskesmas
referral.guide_hero_desc: Many people do not know that psychiatric consultations, psychotherapy, and psychiatric medications are 100% covered by BPJS Health in Indonesia at Puskesmas and regional hospitals.
referral.step1_desc: Go to the Puskesmas or primary clinic listed on your BPJS Health card or Mobile JKN app.
referral.step1_item1: Bring original ID (KTP) & BPJS card / verify active status on Mobile JKN
referral.step1_item2: Take a general outpatient queue ticket at the registration desk
referral.step2_title: 2. Consult General Practitioner & Request Referral Letter
referral.step2_desc: Discuss your psychological symptoms openly with the physician. You have the right to request a psychiatric referral if the facility lacks a mental health specialist.
referral.step2_item1: Use the RIMA Conversation Scripts below if feeling nervous or unsure what to say
referral.step2_item2: Present the RIMA Clinical Handover Brief (PHQ-9/GAD-7 scores & mood timeline)
referral.step2_item3: Ask the doctor to issue an online BPJS Referral Letter (P-Care) to the hospital psychiatric clinic
referral.step3_desc: Visit the designated regional hospital on your referral date to see a Psychiatrist (Sp.KJ) or Clinical Psychologist.
referral.step3_item1: Medical consultation and psychotherapy are fully covered by BPJS
referral.step3_item2: Prescribed psychiatric medications (antidepressants/anxiolytics) in Fornas BPJS are free
referral.step3_item3: Referral letters are generally valid for 3 months for recurring follow-ups
referral.scripts_subtitle: Feeling anxious or unsure how to articulate your feelings? Copy or read one of the structured scripts below to the doctor:
referral.script_depression_text: Good morning/afternoon, Doctor. For the past few weeks, I have been experiencing persistent sadness, severe exhaustion without physical cause, loss of interest, and difficulty sleeping. These symptoms are interfering with my daily functioning. I would like to consult about this and respectfully request a referral to the hospital psychiatric clinic or clinical psychologist for further evaluation.
referral.script_anxiety_text: Doctor, I frequently experience sudden panic and anxiety episodes with chest tightness, rapid heart palpitations, and shaking hands, despite normal physical exams. I feel I need specialized psychiatric care to manage this severe anxiety. Could you please assist in issuing a BPJS referral to the psychiatric clinic?
referral.script_stress_text: Doctor, I am undergoing intense emotional stress that hinders my ability to focus on study/work, feeling hopeless with recurrent negative thoughts. I would like to seek professional psychiatric evaluation and counseling through BPJS. I would appreciate your guidance and referral, Doctor.
referral.handover_title: Print Clinical Handover Brief for Doctor
referral.handover_subtitle: Primary care doctors have limited consultation time. This clean A4 brief summarizes your screening metrics and mood trends for rapid physician triage.
referral.handover_note_placeholder: Add any specific chief complaints you wish to highlight to the physician (optional)...
referral.handover_privacy_notice: This document is processed 100% locally on your device and is never transmitted to external servers.
referral.faq_q1: Are psychiatric medications free under BPJS?
referral.faq_a1: Yes. Psychotropic and antidepressant medications included in the National Formulary (Fornas) are 100% covered by BPJS.
referral.faq_a2: In acute psychiatric emergencies (e.g. acute suicidal thoughts or severe agitation), you can go directly to the nearest Hospital Emergency Room (IGD) without needing a prior Puskesmas referral.
referral.faq_q3: How long is a referral letter valid?
referral.faq_a3: Online referral letters (P-Care) are generally valid for 90 days (3 months) and can be extended by the hospital specialist.
referral.preview_hint: Below is the standardized A4 handover document format to be printed or presented to the examining physician.

sleep.title: Sleep Diary & CBT-I
sleep.subtitle: Structured Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia approach to track sleep efficiency, restructure circadian rhythm, and overcome insomnia medication-free.
sleep.stimulusRuleDesc: If you lie in bed for more than 20 minutes unable to sleep, get out of bed. Move to a dimly lit room and practice soothing activities until sleepiness returns.
sleep.noEntriesDesc: Start recording your bedtimes, sleep latency, and efficiency to gain clinical insight into your sleep architecture.
sleep.tip_stimulus_desc: If you cannot sleep within 20 minutes, get out of bed. Do calming relaxation (Cyclic Sighing or Grounding) in dim light, returning to bed only when truly sleepy.
sleep.tip_wake_desc: Wake up at the exact same time every day, including weekends. This is the strongest physiological anchor for circadian rhythm.
sleep.tip_screen_desc: Avoid smartphones and blue light 60 minutes prior to sleep to trigger natural melatonin release.
sleep.tip_caffeine_desc: Caffeine half-life spans 5 to 7 hours. Cease coffee, strong tea, or energy drinks after 2:00 PM.

moodMeter.quadrant_red_desc: High sympathetic autonomic activation (alert, agitated, panic). Requires rapid somatic down-regulation.
moodMeter.quadrant_red_strategy: Practice Cyclic Sighing or cold TIPP temperature to rapidly decelerate heart rate.
moodMeter.quadrant_yellow_desc: High positive energy state (joyful, inspired). Great moment for creative expression or savoring.
moodMeter.quadrant_yellow_strategy: Savor this positive momentum or write an entry in your gratitude journal.
moodMeter.quadrant_blue_desc: Low emotional energy, depleted, or numb. Avoid isolation and embrace gentle restorative care.
moodMeter.quadrant_blue_strategy: Engage in a low-threshold activity (Behavioral Activation) or 5-4-3-2-1 grounding.
moodMeter.quadrant_green_desc: Optimal parasympathetic rest-and-digest state (calm, serene, content). Ideal for mindful reflection.
moodMeter.quadrant_green_strategy: Maintain tranquility with gentle mindful breathing or spiritual reflection.
moodMeter.nuance_title: Specific Emotion Nuances (Select all that resonate):

audio.headphone_note: Headphones recommended for optimal binaural beat perception.
audio.brown_noise_desc: Gentle low-frequency sound resembling ocean waves to quiet racing thoughts and overstimulation.
audio.theta_binaural_desc: Binaural frequency clinically shown to soothe acute anxiety and down-regulate autonomic arousal.
audio.alpha_binaural_desc: Balances brainwaves during pre-exam jitters, interviews, or cognitive demands.
audio.pink_noise_desc: Balanced octave energy distribution that masks room noise and cultivates tranquility.

cft.step1_sub: Name what you are feeling right now. You do not have to pretend to be strong.
cft.step1_custom_label: Or write what you are experiencing in your own words:
cft.step1_custom_placeholder: e.g. My chest feels tight and heavy because of this...
cft.step2_heading: 2. Common Humanity: You Are Not Alone
cft.step2_sub: Hardship, failure, and imperfection are part of the shared universal human experience.
cft.step3_sub: Gentle physical touch stimulates oxytocin release to soothe your nervous system.
cft.step3_touch_pick: Choose a soothing somatic posture that feels comforting right now:
cft.step3_kindness_pick: Choose a compassionate wish or mantra for yourself:
cft.covenant_blessing: Take one deep breath. Feel the warmth of your touch and allow your heart to soften.
cft.grounding_cta_sub: Try a 3-Step Self-Compassion Break to soften self-blame and give yourself a safe haven.
cft.mindfulness_phrase_1: This is a moment of genuine suffering and exhaustion for me.
cft.mindfulness_phrase_2: This pain, anxiety, or disappointment is real and valid to feel.
cft.mindfulness_phrase_3: I am hurting right now, and I don't need to pretend that I am okay.
cft.humanity_phrase_1: Struggle and failure are part of being human, not evidence of personal defect.
cft.humanity_phrase_2: Many others out there are wrestling with the exact same emotions right now. I am not alone.
cft.humanity_phrase_3: No human is perfect. My mistakes do not define my entire self-worth.
cft.kindness_phrase_1: May I be as gentle, patient, and understanding with myself today as I would with a dear friend.
cft.kindness_phrase_2: May I forgive my limitations and accept myself just as I am.
cft.kindness_phrase_3: May I give myself the time, space, and care needed to rest and heal.
cft.touch_heart_desc: Place one or both hands gently over your chest. Feel their warmth and your faithful heartbeat.
cft.touch_hug_desc: Cross your arms and tenderly embrace your upper arms, like comforting a beloved friend.
cft.touch_cheek_desc: Cup your cheeks with both palms with gentle coolness and total unconditional acceptance.
cft.touch_belly_desc: Rest your hand on your abdomen and feel the rise and fall of each soothing breath.

jitai.red_vagal_desc: Your nervous system activation is elevated. Take a double inhale through your nose followed by a long exhale (Cyclic Sighing) to lower your heart rate.
jitai.drop_recovery_desc: A mood decline has been detected. Take a gentle moment to acknowledge your feelings with warmth and non-judgment.
jitai.blue_spark_desc: Energy is feeling low and heavy right now. Try a gentle 5-minute micro-activity to slowly stimulate dopamine.
jitai.sleep_efficiency_desc: Your sleep efficiency is recorded below 85%. Apply the CBT-I principle: reserve bed strictly for when you feel sleepy.
jitai.sleep_latency_desc: It took over 30 minutes to fall asleep. Reduce screen exposure and start a calming 20-minute wind-down routine.
jitai.sleep_waso_desc: Nighttime awake duration exceeded 30 minutes. If awake for over 20 minutes, get out of bed and engage in a calming dim-light activity.
jitai.inactivity_spark_desc: It has been over 48 hours since your last meaningful activity. Take 5 minutes for one small action bringing mastery or pleasure.
jitai.activity_reminder_desc: You have a scheduled activity planned. Ready to do it now?

safetyCard.title: You Are Not Alone
safetyCard.subtitle: Calm your mind. You are safe here. Choose one immediate action below.
safetyCard.addContactSub: Add a phone number in your Safety Plan
safetyCard.somaticSub: Lower heart rate and soothe acute panic immediately
safetyCard.disclaimer: Toll-free emergency services. If in immediate physical danger, call 112 or visit the nearest emergency room.
